questions.question: 1. When a synchronous motor is running at synchronous speed, the damper winding produces

explanations.a: Correct. Damper winding produces damping torque during oscillations to reduce hunting.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Eddy currents are part of damping but not the primary torque.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Damper winding does not produce driving torque at synchronous speed.

questions.question: 2. The reactance of any machine is ------------- proportional to reluctance of flux path and ---------- proportional to square of number of turns

explanations.a: Correct. Reactance X = 2πfL, and L ∝ N²/Reluctance, so X ∝ N² and X ∝ 1/Reluctance.

questions.question: 3. The armature reactance of salient pole synchronous machine

explanations.a: Incorrect. Armature reactance depends on rotor position.
explanations.c: Correct. Due to saliency, armature reactance varies between Xd and Xq depending on rotor position relative to MMF axis.

questions.question: 4. The ratio of X<sub>d</sub> to X<sub>q</sub> in salient pole machine varies in the range

explanations.a: Incorrect. That is for Xq/Xd, not Xd/Xq.
explanations.c: Incorrect. That is for cylindrical machines.
explanations.d: Correct. For salient pole machines, Xd/Xq typically ranges from 1.0 to 1.5 (or higher up to 2.5 in some cases).

questions.question: 5. By which test synchronous machine can be recognised as cylindrical or salient pole type?

explanations.a: Correct. Slip test reveals whether Xd = Xq (cylindrical) or Xd ≠ Xq (salient pole) by observing armature current and voltage variations.
explanations.c: Incorrect. OC test gives magnetization curve, not reactance ratio.
explanations.d: Incorrect. SC test gives synchronous reactance but not Xd/Xq separately.
